title: 'Breaking Bad' star RJ Mitte mourned by co-stars as official cause of death is confirmed
text:

Using deprecated PresentationRouter. 'Breaking Bad' star RJ Mitte mourned by co-stars as official cause of death is confirmed
 by Elizabeth Stanton
 Tue, October 13th 2026 at 1:18 PM 4 VIEW ALL PHOTOS LOS ANGELES, CA - SEPTEMBER 23: Actors Bryan Cranston and RJ Mitte arrive at the 64th Annual Primetime Emmy Awards at Nokia Theatre L.A. Live on September 23, 2012 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Frazer Harrison/Getty Images) TOPICS:
 RJ Mitte Breaking Bad Cerebral Palsy Suicide Bryan Cranston Aaron Paul Disability rights 988 Lifeline RJ Mitte’s “Breaking Bad” family is mourning the young actor after his death by suicide Monday.
 Bryan Cranston, who played his TV dad Walter White, shared a touching tribute to him on Instagram.
 “I’m in deep despair as I write this tonight. RJ Mitte, my sweet son on ‘Breaking Bad’ has died. I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm,” Cranston wrote. “Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never - ever - allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything. He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination.”
 Cranston continued, “Always listening to the advice that his TV parents (Anna Gunn and myself) gave him - but being a teenager, sometimes mischievously ignoring the counsel in order to learn the hard way He was one of the stars of a hit TV show - but still a kid.”
 The actor praised Mitte’s disability advocacy, lamenting, “All that promise and potential now is such a loss. It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life. Why?”
 Cranston added, “We were texting each other just a few weeks ago - figuring out when we could meet for lunch. I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future
 But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on ‘Breaking Bad’ dimmedI’ll miss you, son.”
 He also encouraged others to seek support at the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
 Mitte’s representative confirmed to PEOPLE that the actor died by suicide. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” they previously confirmed to the outlet.
 His onscreen uncle, Dean Norris, shared on X, “Oh my God! Was working just found out about RJ I am heartbroken Though RJ didn’t play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set. He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed. This is so heartbreaking, I can’t believe it. Thinking of him and his family.”
 “Breaking Bad” star Aaron Paul also spoke on Mitte’s passing, telling The Hollywood Reporter , “I am at a loss. I am heartbroken over this news. RJ, I love you my friend. You will be missed. And to whoever happens to be reading this, please know you are loved, and you are not alone. Always remember that.”
 Mitte played Walter White Jr., a.k.a Flynn, the son of Cranston’s meth cooking kingpin Walter White on the hit series for all six seasons.
 He was diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy at the age of three and played characters with the condition, including Walt Jr, though he exaggerated some of his own symptoms to authentically play a more severe presentation of CP on the show.
 RJ Mitte served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s as well as the president of The Mitte Foundation, which supports philanthropic efforts and community initiatives.
 If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.
